description: Negotiation Table tell corpus. One terse, data-defined posture line per stance x trust band. The player reads the trader the way the trader reads the offer. Rotation is seed-deterministic via ISeededRng. Tone: cold, exhausted, human, restrained. No modern slang, no anachronisms, no fourth-wall breaks.

hostile: The table is a formality. Their hands never leave the rifle slings.
They have already decided what they are taking. The barter is theater.
Nobody sits on your side of the table anymore.
wary: They count your people before they count your goods.
The sentries shift when you reach for your pack.
Every answer comes through gritted teeth.
neutral: They talk trade, but the perimeter crews keep drilling.
The ledger is open and the knives are not put away.
A raid is being priced somewhere behind those eyes.
warm: Old debts keep the peace, barely. The ledger stays open.
They still trade like a friend, and watch you like weather.
The greeting is warm. The exit stays covered.

hostile: Whatever you set down, they intend to keep. All of it.
They weigh your pack, not your offer.
The quartermaster's fingers drum the counter like a countdown.
wary: Their eyes do the arithmetic on everything you carry.
Goods change hands here. Fairness was never on the table.
They ask what else is in the shelter, twice.
neutral: The stall is open, but the scale is loaded.
They nod along to your terms while repositioning the guard.
Whatever you agree to, expect less back.
warm: Habit, not hunger, keeps their hands moving toward your goods.
They short you gently, almost apologetically.
Old affection buys you a smaller theft than most.

hostile: The stall shutter is down. It does not open for you.
They fold their arms and wait for you to understand.
Nothing you carry is worth the conversation.
wary: The quartermaster barely glances at your offer.
They wave you off before you finish unpacking.
Come back with more than noise, they say, and mean never.
neutral: The shutter is half-open. Not today, they say. Not to you.
They listen to the whole offer, then shake their heads once.
The door stays closed, but they let you finish your sentence.
warm: They refuse softly, saving you the humiliation of arguing.
Not the goods, they say. The timing. Come back after the thaw.
They pour you something warm and trade nothing at all.

hostile: The deal is real. The hands holding it are not steady.
They trade like men settling an estate nobody wanted.
Business is done quickly, and nobody turns their back.
wary: Every item is counted twice, once out loud for your benefit.
They keep one hand on the ledger and one near the door.
The terms are fair and the tone is not.
neutral: The quartermaster works down the list without hurry.
They weigh the goods, then weigh you, then decide.
A plain deal at a plain table. Nothing wasted, nothing given.
warm: They push the good items toward your side of the table first.
The count runs in your favor and nobody corrects it.
Coffee appears, black and thin, before the haggling starts.

hostile: They trade, they talk, and none of it can be trusted twice.
The intel comes fast and cheap, like they want you gone.
Every warning they share is also a test of what you fear.
wary: The goods are fair. The information arrives in pieces.
They tell you just enough to learn what you already know.
Advice is free here. Acting on it is not.
neutral: Between items, they mention which roads are closed.
The ledger closes and the real conversation begins.
They mark the fallout drift on your map without being asked.
warm: They set the ledger aside and speak to you like kin.
You get the news before the radio does, some nights.
They warn you about the crossing two days before the convoy burns.
